median_wage_source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), May 2023 State Occupational Employment and Wage Estimates - Tennessee, 2024, https://www.bls.gov/oes/current/oes_tn.htm
license_regime: In Tennessee, contractor licensing is regulated at the state level by the Tennessee Board for Licensing Contractors (under the Department of Commerce and Insurance). A state contractor license is required for any project or subcontract valued at $25,000 or more (labor and materials combined); work under $25,000 is governed by local municipal/county permitting or Home Improvement licensing rules. Glass and glazing work is classified under specialty trade BC-6 (Glass, Window and Door Construction), or under broader general classifications such as BC (General Building) or BC-B (Commercial Construction). Specialty subcontractors are only required to hold a state contractor license if their portion of the project equals or exceeds $25,000. License tiers (monetary limits) are established based on verified financial statements (net worth/working capital) or surety bonds and set project value ceilings (e.g., up to $500,000; $500,001 to $1,500,000 for BC-b small commercial; and $1,500,001+ for unlimited).

license_regime: A state-level license issued by the Construction Industries Division (CID) of the New Mexico Regulation and Licensing Department is required for contracting work exceeding $7,200 per year under the Construction Industries Licensing Act (NMSA 1978, § 60-13-1 et seq.). License classifications include General Building (GB-2 Residential, GB-98 General Building) and Building Specialty (GS classifications).

license_regime: State-level licensing is required for remediation/mold contractors under New York State Labor Law Article 32, administered by the New York State Department of Labor (NYSDOL) Division of Safety and Health. Article 32 establishes four licensing tiers: Mold Assessor, Mold Remediation Contractor, Mold Abatement Worker Supervisor, and Mold Abatement Worker. license_regime: In North Dakota, a statewide contractor license issued by the Secretary of State is legally required for any commercial or residential construction, repair, alteration, or restoration work when a single project contract value is $4,000 or more (NDCC § 43-07-02). license_regime: Pennsylvania does not issue a state-level restoration or general contractor trade license. However, under the Home Improvement Consumer Protection Act (HICPA), Act 132 of 2008 (73 P.S. § 517.1 et seq.), any contractor performing residential restoration, remediation, or home improvement work valued at $5,000 or more annually (or on contracts exceeding $500) must register as a Home Improvement Contractor (HIC) with the Pennsylvania Office of Attorney General. Detailed trade licenses (e.g., electrical, plumbing, HVAC) are regulated at the municipal/county level (such as in Philadelphia and Pittsburgh).

Laws § 5-65 through the Rhode Island Contractors' Registration and Licensing Board (RICRLB). While a trade-specific restoration license does not exist, all general contractors and subcontractors operating in residential or commercial construction must register with RICRLB. First-time applicants performing work on residential structures must complete a state-approved 5-hour pre-registration education course.

Licensing for general contractors is divided into five financial tiers: Group 1 (up to $100,000), Group 2 (up to $400,000), Group 3 (up to $1,000,000), Group 4 (up to $3,000,000), and Group 5 (Unlimited).

license_regime: State-level contractor licensing is required in Tennessee under TCA Title 62, Chapter 6, administered by the Board for Licensing Contractors within the Tennessee Department of Commerce and Insurance (TDCI). Projects valued at $25,000 or more require a General Contractor License (with a Specialty/Environmental classification or S-Mold designation).
